description: n512 B640: fuse panel-factor + trailing-apply into one persistent warp-specialized megakernel in CUDA C++/CUTE DSL on sm_100a. Use a producer/consumer split (TMA/async-copy warps stage panel and trailing tiles into SMEM while tcgen05 MMA warps consume), software-pipelined across outer blocks, so the whole n512 QR for a CTA's matrices runs in a single launch with no global round-trips between panel and trailing GEMM. Attacks the 51% qr_panel_apply launch-and-reload overhead directly.

Trial 1: OB-megakernel qr_ob_inner_mega_kernel fuses an outer block's 4 inner sub-panels (panel-factor + WMMA inner-apply) into ONE launch via extracted paf_panel_phase/paf_apply_phase device helpers (refactored from qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel; the standalone PAF still builds+is byte-identical). Wired via a new try_ob_fuse hook in run_two_level_loop, gated by g_ob_mega set in set_n512_good_flags. Builds clean. eval test shapes PASS (n512 B<=16 route to geqrf, not the mega path), but the diff_correctness + invariance guards FAIL with NaN/Inf at the n512 B640 benchmark shapes (3/7/9/10): the mega kernel is missing an inter-sub-panel global-memory barrier (apply j writes C to global, panel j+1 reads it without a __syncthreads fence). Fix next.

Trial 2: OB-megakernel now CORRECT (added a CTA-scoped __syncthreads fence at the end of paf_apply_phase so each sub-panel's global C writes publish before the next sub-panel's panel load). validate PASS incl all 3 problem-specific guards. Benchmark geomean=1702.5us, a +3.7% REGRESSION vs 1641.6 baseline. Per-shape: n512 dense s3 3683us (+16% vs 3164), rankdef s9 3150 (+19%), clustered s10 2322 (+17%); but mixed s7 4930us (-3% vs 5090). Diagnosis: collapsing 24 inner PAF launches->8 OB launches is net-negative because (1) the standalone PAF's per-launch gap let the scheduler overlap OTHER matrices' CTAs, lost when one CTA runs the whole OB serially; (2) the mega kernel sizes dynamic smem to the FIRST (largest-m_i) sub-panel for the whole OB, so the smaller later sub-panels run at the worst-case occupancy instead of their own higher occupancy. DRAM is only 12% used so reload elimination is not the lever; barriers+occupancy are. Next: pursue warp-specialized pipelining (overlap panel j+1 factor with apply j) -- the real fix for the barrier-bound regime the ncu profile shows (5.5cyc barrier stall, 1.1 eligible warps).

Trial 3: OB-mega HYBRID via g_ob_mega_maxm=384 -- fuse only the later small-m_o outer blocks (m_o<=384, ko>=128) into the megakernel, keep the first two big OBs (m_o=512,448) on the per-sub-panel PAF path. Hypothesis: fusion's launch-savings pay off where occupancy is rich (small OBs) and hurt where occupancy is constrained (big OBs). validate PASS. geomean=1678.1us, +2.2% vs 1641.6 baseline (BETTER than full-mega's 1702 but still a regression). n512 dense s3=3489us (+10% vs 3164), rankdef s9=2928 (+10%). Hypothesis FALSIFIED: even small-OB fusion regresses -- the standalone PAF's per-sub-panel occupancy (each sub-panel sized to its own smaller m_i) plus the cross-matrix launch-gap overlap (640 matrices fill the SM during each launch boundary) dominates the saved launch latency. Trend is monotonic: less fusion = less regression, so for this occupancy-rich shape the no-fusion baseline is the local optimum of this mechanism. Still open: (a) band-resident mega (literal no-global-round-trips, but predicted worse by occupancy); (b) cp.async/TMA-pipelined apply mainloop (overlap C tile staging with MMA -- helps the apply WITHOUT changing launch structure, applies to standalone PAF too); (c) the FULL single-launch megakernel incl in-kernel outer applies.

Trial 4: BAND-RESIDENT OB-megakernel qr_ob_band_mega_kernel -- the literal brief 'no global round-trips between panel and trailing GEMM'. Stages the whole OB band [ko:n,ko:obe] (m_o x ob bf16) into SMEM once, runs ALL inner sub-panels (panel-factor + WMMA apply) ENTIRELY on the SMEM band (no_csh=1 reads C from the band, no_vsh=0 keeps V in smem Vsh), writes the band back to global ONCE. Generalized paf_panel_phase/paf_apply_phase with ldA/aroff/acoff + Cmat/ldC/crow/ccol params so ONE code path drives both global (byte-identical) and SMEM-band. validate PASS incl all guards. geomean=1743.9us, +6.2% vs 1641.6 (WORST of the 3 fusion variants). n512 dense s3=3844us (+22% vs 3164), rankdef s9=3349 (+26%), mixed s7=5337 (+5%). At ko=0 the band(64KB)+Vsh(16KB)+panel-pool(32KB)=112KB caps the kernel to ~2 CTA/SM (vs standalone PAF's 5 at 32.9KB). Since the parent ncu showed DRAM at only 12% (memory-idle), eliminating the OB-internal HBM round-trips bought ~nothing on the critical path while the 5->2 CTA/SM occupancy loss dominated. CONFIRMS the bottleneck is OCCUPANCY (and the SIMT panel barrier chain), NOT memory traffic -- so every variant that raises resident SMEM to cut HBM traffic moves the wrong lever for this occupancy-rich (B=640, 740 CTAs at 5/SM) shape. Still open: variants that DON'T raise smem -- (a) cp.async double-buffered panel band load (overlap next-column dequant w/ current reduction, smem-neutral); (b) reducing the panel's per-column __syncthreads count (the 33%-barrier-stall root); (c) the FULL single-launch megakernel incl in-kernel outer applies (eliminates the 7 cuBLAS outer-apply + 7 build_Minv launches too -- a different launch-count lever).

Trial 5: inner-mega (global-resident) with g_ob_mega_maxm=192 -- fuse ONLY the 3 smallest, most-occupancy-rich late outer blocks (m_o<=192: ko=320/384/448) into one launch each, keep the 5 bigger OBs (m_o>=256) on the per-sub-panel standalone PAF. geomean=1647.0us, +0.33% vs 1641.6 (WITHIN run noise ~0.15-1%). Per-shape vs baseline: n512 dense s3=3280us (+3.7%, vs full-mega's +16% and hybrid-384's +10%), rankdef s9=2692 (+1.5%), clustered s10=1953 (-2.0% FASTER), mixed s7=5020 (-1.4% FASTER). This maps the fusion sweep cleanly: regression shrinks monotonically as the fused set is restricted to smaller/occupancy-richer OBs (full +3.7% -> maxm384 +2.2% -> maxm192 +0.33%), and on the small-batch-good-subset shapes (clustered/mixed) fusing the small OBs is a small WIN. The crossover is ~m_o<=192. So the launch-fusion megakernel is break-even-to-slightly-positive ONLY for the small-OB / lower-occupancy tail; for the big occupancy-rich OBs the standalone PAF's cross-matrix launch-gap overlap wins. Next: sweep maxm=128 to find the positive-side optimum, and try fusing small OBs at HELP=2.

Trial 6: inner-mega maxm=128 (fuse only the 2 smallest OBs, m_o<=128: ko=384,448). validate PASS (all guards CLEAN). geomean A/B = 1636.6 then 1640.3us, averaging ~1638 ~= baseline 1641.6 (BREAK-EVEN, within ~0.3% run noise). Per-shape stable across both runs: n512 dense s3=3227us (+2.0% vs 3164), rankdef s9=2630 (-0.8%), clustered s10=1951 (-2.0%), mixed s7=5039 (-1.0%). Completes the maxm sweep: full +3.7% -> 384 +2.2% -> 192 +0.33% -> 128 break-even. The OB-inner-megakernel is tunable to NEUTRAL (the small-OB regression offsets the capped-loop-shape gains) but does NOT clear a win for the occupancy-rich n512 dense, because the standalone PAF's cross-matrix launch-gap overlap + per-sub-panel occupancy is already near-optimal for B=640. The fusion's value is real but small and concentrated on the lower-occupancy capped-loop shapes (rankdef/clustered ncap<512, fewer/smaller OBs) and the mixed good-subset (fewer matrices). DIRECTIONS STILL OPEN for the manager: (1) fuse small OBs at HELP=2 (the codebase already found HELP=2 helps the capped loop -- it may stack with small-OB fusion on rankdef/clustered); (2) the full single-launch megakernel incl in-kernel WIDE outer apply is INFEASIBLE in smem (w=64,rest=448 needs >228KB with V resident -- that is exactly why it is on cuBLAS) so that headline variant is library-dominated; (3) the profile-confirmed real bottleneck is the SIMT panel barrier chain (33% barrier stall, 1.1 eligible warps at 51% occ) -- a panel that needs fewer per-column __syncthreads or routes the column reductions onto tensor cores would attack the actual critical path, but that is a panel-rewrite brief, not a fusion brief.

Trial 7 (BREAKTHROUGH): inner-mega with g_ob_mega_maxm=384 + g_ob_mega_minb=5. The ncu profile of the fused inner-mega (trial 6) showed it used 64 regs/thread (vs the standalone PAF's 48), capping occupancy to 41.6% (vs 51.5%) -- THE reason fusion only broke even. Adding __launch_bounds__(NWARPS*32, MINB=5) forces ptxas to fit 5 CTAs/SM (~51 regs, ~PAF), restoring occupancy while keeping the launch-fusion savings. Result: geomean A/B = 1632.3 then 1631.0us (agree within 0.08%), a stable -0.6% WIN vs 1641.6 baseline -- the FIRST genuine improvement. Per-shape (reproducible across both runs): n512 dense s3=3118-3125us (-1.2% vs 3164), rankdef s9=2611 (-1.5%), clustered s10=1947 (-2.2%), mixed s7=5014 (-1.5%); the n=1024/2048/4096 + small-n shapes unchanged (mega gated to n512). All 3 problem-specific guards CLEAN. So the OB-inner-megakernel (fuse each outer block's inner sub-panels into one launch) DOES beat the per-sub-panel PAF once the fused kernel's register footprint is capped to preserve occupancy. Next: sweep maxm=0 (fuse ALL OBs incl the biggest) and minb=6 to find the optimum.

Trial 8: inner-mega maxm=0 (fuse ALL outer blocks incl m_o=512,448) + minb=5. geomean=1648.0us, +0.4% vs baseline -- WORSE than trial 7's maxm=384 (1631). Even with the register cap, fusing the two BIGGEST OBs regresses: n512 dense s3=3179us (vs 3125 at maxm384), clustered s10=2012 (vs 1947), rankdef s9=2661 (vs 2611). At m_o=512 the panel FP32 scratch (~32KB) keeps smem high and the cross-matrix launch-gap overlap is most valuable for the longest-running big-OB launches, so standalone PAF wins there. Confirms maxm=384 (the first 2 OBs on standalone PAF, the later 6 fused) is the optimum boundary. Reverting maxm to 384 for the next minb sweep.

Trial 9: inner-mega maxm=384 + minb=6 (vs trial 7's minb=5). geomean=1638.6us, worse than minb=5's 1631-1632. The tighter __launch_bounds__ minBlocksPerSM=6 (~42 regs, 6 CTA/SM theoretical) forces register SPILLS whose latency outweighs the extra occupancy; n512 dense s3=3166us (vs 3125 at minb5), clustered s10=1976 (vs 1947). So minb=5 (~51 regs ~= PAF's 48, 5 CTA/SM, no spill) is the register-cap sweet spot. Optimum config = maxm=384 + minb=5 = -0.6%. Reverting minb to 5 for the maxm fine-sweep.

Trial 10: inner-mega maxm=256 + minb=5. geomean=1635.8us, slightly worse than trial 7's maxm=384 (1631-1632). Keeping the 3rd OB (m_o=384) on standalone PAF (maxm=256) instead of fusing it costs ~0.3%, so m_o=384 SHOULD be fused. maxm=384 + minb=5 confirmed as the optimum. Full maxm sweep at minb=5: maxm=0(all)=1648, 256=1636, 384=1631(PEAK), and at minb=1: 192=1647, 128=1638. Reverting to the maxm=384+minb=5 winner as the final state.

Trial 11 (FINAL/optimum): OB-inner-megakernel maxm=384 + minb=5. geomean=1630.3us (3rd confirming run A/B/C=1632.3/1631.0/1630.3, agree within 0.1%), a stable -0.7% WIN vs 1641.6 baseline. validate PASS (all 3 problem-specific guards CLEAN). PROFILED (nsys+ncu, saved as brief-5-trial-11-<sha>.{nsys,ncu}-{rep,txt}): ncu confirms minb=5 capped the fused kernel from 64->48 regs, lifting achieved occupancy 41.6%->49.7% (~=PAF's 51.5%) and eligible-warps 0.97->1.23 (>PAF's 1.1); compute SM 36%->50%. nsys confirms the 24 inner PAF launches dropped to 6 qr_ob_inner_mega + 6 residual PAF (the 2 biggest OBs) = 12 inner launches. n512 dense s3=3124us (-1.3% vs 3164), rankdef s9=2613 (-1.5%), clustered s10=1947 (-2.2%), mixed s7=5018 (-1.5%); n>=1024 + small-n unchanged (mega gated to n512). The brief's launch-fusion mechanism WORKS once the fused kernel's register footprint is capped to preserve occupancy -- the register bloat (not launches/reloads/memory) was the real obstacle for occupancy-rich n512 B640.

Best committed = 1b3cabef0db0660e6c4c2846016af76c204129f7, geomean 1630.3us (A/B/C 1632.3/1631.0/1630.3, agree within 0.1%) vs 1641.6 baseline; validate PASS (all 3 guards); profiled (brief-5-trial-11-<sha>.{nsys,ncu}-{rep,txt}).

WHAT WON: a qr_ob_inner_mega_kernel that fuses each outer block's 4 inner sub-panels (panel-factor + WMMA inner-apply, via paf_panel_phase/paf_apply_phase device helpers extracted byte-identically from qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel) into ONE launch, applied to the LATER 6 OBs (m_o<=384 via g_ob_mega_maxm=384; the 2 biggest OBs stay on standalone PAF) WITH __launch_bounds__ minBlocksPerSM=5 (g_ob_mega_minb). nsys: the 24 inner PAF launches -> 6 mega + 6 residual PAF. n512 dense 3124us (-1.3%), rankdef -1.5%, clustered -2.2%, mixed -1.5%. n>=1024 + small-n untouched (gated to n512).

THE KEY FINDING (profile-driven, 11 trials): the obstacle was NOT launches/reloads/memory -- a naive full-OB fusion REGRESSED +3.7% (band-resident 'no global round-trips' was WORST at +6.2% with DRAM at 3.5% but occupancy halved to 23%). ncu showed the fused kernel bloats to 64 regs/thread (vs PAF's 48), capping occupancy to 41.6%. Capping registers via minb=5 (->48 regs, 49.7% occ, eligible-warps 1.23 > PAF's 1.1) is what turned fusion into a win. Sweeps: maxm {0=1648,256=1636,384=1631(peak),192=1647,128=1638}; minb {6=1639(spills),5=1631(peak,no spill)}.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (please keep going): (1) the win is small (-0.7%) and concentrated on n512 -- the residual standalone PAF (the 2 biggest OBs, m_o=512/448) is still 19.6% of the dense timeline; a register-capped mega that ALSO works for the big OBs (maybe at a different warp count, or no_vsh=0 to cut the big-OB Vg traffic) could extend the win. (2) the FULL single-launch megakernel (incl in-kernel WIDE outer apply) is INFEASIBLE via the existing machinery -- w=64,rest=448 with V resident needs >228KB smem, which is exactly why the outer apply is on cuBLAS; only a from-scratch streaming/TMA GEMM mainloop could do it (library-territory, likely not worth it). (3) the profile-confirmed deepest bottleneck is still the SIMT panel barrier chain (the panel-factor phase) -- a panel that needs fewer per-column __syncthreads, or routes the Householder column reductions onto tensor cores (the brief's tcgen05 hint), would attack the actual critical path and is orthogonal to this fusion win -- worth a dedicated panel-rewrite brief. (4) HELP=2 is already inherited by the mega for the rankdef/clustered capped-loop shapes; a finer per-OB HELP schedule inside the mega (cooperate on the long early-OB m-passes, not the short late ones) is untried. The minb register-cap technique itself is reusable and could help other briefs' fused kernels.

Trial 12: TENSOR-CORE PANEL paf_panel_phase_tc (the brief's unrealized half) -- factor a w-wide panel as SB=16 serial Householder sub-blocks, then apply each sub-block's compact-WY reflector to the panel's remaining columns via WMMA (S=V^T V, M=T^-1 fwd-sub, W=V^T C, Y=M^T W, C-=V Y over m), so the m-direction reflector work runs on FP16 tensor cores instead of the SIMT/LSU rank-1 chain. Builds; eval test shapes PASS (n512 B<=16 routes to geqrf, not this path). FAILS the invariance guard at n512 B640: factor residual ~62 vs allowed ~0.55 (~100x off, NOT NaN) -- the WMMA inter-block apply has a math bug (candidate: the Y=M^T W triangular contraction indexing, the C-=V Y sign/orientation, or the unit-lower V staging). Note this also surfaced the predicted occupancy concern: at IB=32 the FP32 column-major panel s is 32*513*4=65KB, much larger than IB=16's 32KB. Debugging the residual next.

Trial 13: TENSOR-CORE PANEL paf_panel_phase_tc, now CORRECT (the bug was Y=M^T W; reference does Y=M W -- M=T^T is lower-tri so Y[p][q]=sum_{i<=p} M[p][i] W[i][q]) and gated to the DENSE n512 path only (the rank-reveal capped loop rankdef/clustered keeps the all-FP32 SIMT panel via apply_n512_rr_overrides g_panel_tc=0, since BF16 WMMA trailing loses the factor residual on ill-cond columns -- validated, residual ~169). validate PASS (all 3 guards CLEAN). geomean=1672.9us, +2.6% vs the 1630 fusion winner -- a REGRESSION. n512 dense s3=3767us (+20% vs 3124), mixed s7=5492 (+9%). ncu CONFIRMS the mechanism AND the wall: the TC panel DID move m-work to tensor cores (Mem-Pipes/LSU dropped 35%->20%), BUT it needs IB=32 (so a 16-wide WMMA inter-block trailing exists), which makes the FP32 column-major panel s = 32*513*4 = 65KB -> 85KB total dynamic smem -> Block-Limit-Shared-Mem=2 -> occupancy 25%/23.4% (vs the fusion winner's 49.7%). Registers stayed 48 (minb=5 held). So the LSU win is real but the FP32-SMEM-panel-width-for-WMMA forces an occupancy collapse that dominates. THE WALL: WMMA's 16-wide tile floor requires a >=32-wide panel; the panel's FP32 column-major scratch at that width is too big for occupancy. Next: try a BF16 panel s (32KB at w=32, not 65KB) with FP32-accumulated reductions to escape the smem wall.

THREE ncu profiles pin the root cause: the TC panel DID move work off LSU (Mem-Pipes 35%->20%), but the on-chip-WMMA SCRATCH (BF16 V/C tiles + FP32 S/M/W/Wacc, ~28KB) is the new occupancy limiter -> 60KB total -> occ 49.7%->28.7%, and the inter-block trailing is too SMALL (8x8) for the tensor-core throughput to pay for that SMEM + the FP32<->BF16 conversions + extra syncs.

DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING for the n512 group: the panel's SIMT floor is two parts -- (a) the per-column m-reductions + 16 per-column BARRIERS (31% stall, UNCHANGED by any tensor-core variant -- inherently serial Householder), and (b) the rank-1 trailing-column updates (the offloadable LSU). The EXISTING IB=16 + BF16-WMMA inner-apply already offloads the INTER-16-block trailing to tensor cores; the within-block trailing is <16 wide. My TC panel offloads that within-block trailing too, but the SMEM scratch cost exceeds the gain. So 'put the panel on tensor cores' has been TAKEN AS FAR AS WMMA/padded-N=8 allows, and it does not beat the SIMT panel for this occupancy-rich (B=640) shape -- the barrier half of the floor is the true wall, and NO MMA primitive touches it.

ONE PATH LEFT UNBUILT (surfaced for the manager, infra in place + disabled): RAW mma.m16n8k16 PTX (native N=8, no 16-padding) would ~halve the TC scratch (Cbf/S/M/W go 8-wide -> ~14KB vs 28KB -> ~46KB total -> maybe 4 CTA/SM). It MIGHT flip the SB=8 verdict, but my measurements predict it still loses (the barrier-half floor is untouched, the inter-block work is tiny, and 4 CTA/SM < the fusion winner's 5). It is a large, error-prone fragment-layout build; I judged building a 3rd TC variant I have strong measured evidence will regress lower-value than returning these results. The g_panel_tc/g_panel_tc_sb infra makes it a localized swap for a dedicated brief. Other directions: TSQR/CAQR for the tall m=512 panel (attacks the m-reduction directly, but changes the (H,tau) reconstruction); a barrier-count reduction in the SIMT panel (the 31% stall the MMA work can't touch). Net: the fusion -0.5% is the real, validated, profiled win; the tensor-core panel is proven (built+correct+profiled) to regress for a precisely-characterized occupancy reason.
